LESSON: READING COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: READING 2.1 Independent By the end of the sub-strand, the  Learners guess the m
Topic 2.2: Reading comprehension

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Reading comprehension. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read with accuracy, fluency, and 5 lessons
2. read through texts to make personal judgments or opinions on the subjects of the text
3. locate information in a text
4. use acquired words to form sentences and read them accurately at an appropriate speed e) develop an interest in reading widely on varied subjects

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. read with accuracy, fluency, and 5 lessons
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to read with accuracy, fluency, and 5 lessons. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. read through texts to make personal judgments or opinions on the subjects of the text
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to read through texts to make personal judgments or opinions on the subjects of the text. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. locate information in a text
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to locate information in a text. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

4. use acquired words to form sentences and read them accurately at an appropriate speed e) develop an interest in reading widely on varied subjects
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to use acquired words to form sentences and read them accurately at an appropriate speed e) develop an interest in reading widely on varied subjects. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Reading comprehension.
2. Explain Reading comprehension to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading comprehension.
4. Show that you can: read with accuracy, fluency, and 5 lessons
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading comprehension. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Reading comprehension important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. read with accuracy, fluency, and 5 lessons
2. read through texts to make personal judgments or opinions on the subjects of the text
3. locate information in a text
4. use acquired words to form sentences and read them accurately at an appropriate speed e) develop an interest in reading widely on varied subjects

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
